reason: E1 directly supports the strength-ductility synergy via coherent nanoprecipitates and the SCCP concept. E2 and E3 demonstrate that refractory HEAs can have high strength and energetic release, but neither provides evidence that a precipitation treatment preserves or does not harm energy release behavior, which is a key unsupported premise.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in refractory HEAs by facilitating dislocation transmission and relieving stress concentrations.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation (SCCP) is a viable processing route to achieve such a microstructure.
Refractory HEAs can serve as energetic structural materials with high strength and impact-induced energy release.
The proposed thermo-mechanical treatment will preserve the intrinsic energy release characteristics of the alloy.
